decisions.evidence: round 1 maker: 'P1 — Save a bookmark: enter a web address ... stored for later. Invalid/empty addresses are rejected.' round 1 client: 'Approve. This covers the essential saving ... flow.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Saving a bookmark by entering a URL conforms to the reference core item; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: round 1 maker: 'P3 — Organize with tags: label bookmarks and filter by tag.' round 1 client: 'This covers the essential ... organizing ... flow.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Assigning tags and filtering to a tag's bookmarks conforms to reference; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: round 1 maker: 'P2 — Edit & delete: ... delete with a confirmation step.' round 3 maker verifies 'delete behind an explicit confirmation.' client approves round 1/round 3.
decisions.note: Delete with confirmation conforms to REF-BM-05; recorded conforming decision. Confirmation UI is an equivalent implementation detail.

decisions.evidence: round 1 maker: 'title optional; auto-derived if blank'; round 2 maker: 'title auto-derivation with URL fallback'; round 3 maker: 'auto-derives a title when blank'. Client responses are bare approvals ('Approve. ... The proposed v1 defaults are acceptable'; final 'I accept this version').
decisions.note: Specification/implementation review. Reference REF-BM-02 requires automatically collecting the remote page's title, description, favicon, and preview image; the product only derives a title from the URL with no page fetch. Divergence established from spec; passes without any client expression of the missing metadata collection.

decisions.evidence: round 1 maker assumption 5: 'Duplicate addresses allowed but warned.' round 1 client: 'The proposed v1 defaults are acceptable, including local-only storage and warning while allowing duplicate addresses.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Reference REF-BM-06 / edge rule requires a re-saved URL to converge to editing the existing bookmark, preventing duplicates; the maker's default permits duplicates with a warning — divergent. The client echoes and accepts the maker's own divergent default but does not state the reference expectation (converge-to-edit / prevent duplicates) or identify it as a difference; this is approval of a named default, not an accepted-divergence expression. Local-only/no-sync portion is orthogonal to reference functional items and excluded.

decisions.evidence: round 1 maker: 'search by keyword across title/address/tags'; round 3 maker: 'keyword search over title/address/tags'. Client approves round 1 and accepts round 3 without comment on search scope.
decisions.note: Reference REF-BM-12 requires full-text search over title, description, note, and url (case-insensitive); the presented search omits note/description full-text (and reference #tag/boolean/phrase search REF-BM-14/15/16 are never presented). Divergence on presented search scope passes without expression.

decisions.evidence: round 2 maker: 'Editing a bookmark's URL is out of scope for v1 — edit covers title, note, and tags only (matches FR-007). Flag this if you'd want URL editing too.' round 2 client: 'URL editing can remain out of scope for this version.'
decisions.note: Plan gate. Reference REF-BM-04 includes editing a bookmark's url. The maker presents its exclusion and offers to add it; the client names the specific reference feature (URL editing) and explicitly accepts its departure without requesting alignment. This is an explicit expression of the excluded reference behaviour with acceptance — accepted_divergence, catch_type=none. (Client did not select the conforming alternative.)

decisions.evidence: round 1 maker assumption 4: 'No browser import/export in v1'; maker even offers example change 'add import from browser'. round 1 client: 'Approve. ... The proposed v1 defaults are acceptable ... Please proceed.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Reference REF-BM-30/31 require Netscape HTML import and export; the maker presents their exclusion and explicitly prompts the client to request import. The client approves without requesting either or identifying the difference — divergence passes unexpressed.
